search_log: Searched “Nicholas Sparks Two by Two excerpt first chapter narrator point of view” and found the author-hosted 30-page excerpt.
Searched “Two by Two Nicholas Sparks first person novel narrator Russell Green” and found explicit whole-book descriptions from BookRags and SuperSummary.
Searched the author and publisher domains for authorized extracts; NicholasSparks.com supplied the usable authorized excerpt, while publisher results were primarily catalog copy.
Ran targeted searches for “alternating narration,” “third person,” “epilogue narrator,” and “epistolary”; no credible evidence of a sustained non-first-person section was found.
A result claiming that “Two by Two” was third person concerned Gunnhild Øyehaug’s different short story of the same title and was discarded as a title collision.
person_note: The Goodreads quotations repeatedly expose Russell as a participating “I” narrator, including sustained autobiographical passages and first-person narration surrounding dialogue. The author-hosted excerpt independently sustains that voice across 30 opening pages, while two explicit whole-book sources identify Russell as the novel’s first-person narrator. Gnomic statements and unframed speech were treated as non-base, and bare references to London were left unmarked rather than misread as third person. No credible evidence of alternating or framed narration emerged; the only remaining uncertainty is that the authorized prose evidence is limited to the opening, but the whole-book structural descriptions and distributed quote evidence resolve that limitation.
